To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the glycosylation reactivity of the 4-OMet, 4-OMethoxy, 4-ODechloro and 4-ODefluoro trichloroacetyl donors follows the ranking 4-OMef > 4-OMech ≈ 4-ODeclo > 4-ODEflu, 2) the glycosyl accepter O-4 position can be selectively glycosylated using the BF3·Et
we have synthesized the first analogues of the 4-O-methyl, 4-chloro and 4-fluoro derivatives of Lewis X.
4”-modified Lex analogues were prepared in good overall yields, starting from 1,2-protected galactosyl and glucosamine donors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of three new Lex trisacchardie analogues.
the synthesis of 4”-substituted Lex trisaccheride analogues.
the synthesis of the Lex trimeric antigen in which the 4-OH of the galactoside residue is replaced by a methoxy, a chloro, or a fluoro group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4” methoxy analogue is the least reactive of the three analogues, while the 4” deoxyfluoro is the most reactive.
the 4-OAc analogue is the most reactive, the 4-OH the least, and the 4-OMet, 4-CH2OH, 4-CHO and 4-CHF2 analogues fall between these two.
the glycosylation reaction of the 4-OAc donor is more reactive than those of the 4-F and 4-OMet donors, but less reactive than that of the 4-Cl donor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 4” methoxy, chloro or fluoro analogues of the Lewis X trisacccharide antigen were prepared in good yields.
the 4” deoxyfluoro analogue is a better mimic of the native Lex trisaccheride than the 4”deoxychloro analogue.
the 4-OMethoxy analogue was more reactive than the 4-deoxychloro and less reactive than the 3-deoxyfluoro analogues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycosidation at O-4 is a very sensitive process, and the presence of a halogen atom in the 4” position of Lex is a very good strategy for the synthesis of the Lex antigen.

the 4” position of the Lex tridecasaccharide is not essential for the binding of the antigen to E-selectin, and the 4” methoxy, chloro and fluoro modifications do not interfere with the binding of the Lex trichloroacetonitrile donor to the E-selectin.
the 4-OMethoxy, 4-Deoxychloro and Deoxyfluoro Lex analogues can be synthesized in high yields.
